chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ja'far ibn Muhammad al-Ash'ari, from Ibn al-Qaddah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
Luqman said to his son: 'O my son! If you claim that speech is of silver, then silence is of gold.'

key_terms.لُقْمَانُ: Luqman the Wise, a biblical and Quranic figure known for his wisdom

ai.seo_question: What is the significance of silence compared to speech in Islamic ethics?
ai.summary: This narration, transmitted through the chain of the Ahl al-Bayt in al-Kafi, elevates Luqman’s wisdom by linking it directly to Imam al-Sadiq, thereby grounding the proverb in Shia theological tradition. It underscores the concept of 'hifz al-lisan' (guarding the tongue) as a critical component of spiritual discipline, where silence is not merely absence of speech but an active, gold-standard virtue that prevents sin and preserves dignity.
